description: African padauk is a bright orange-red hardwood that darkens to reddish brown with age. Woodworkers use it for turnery, carving, boxes, accents, flooring and boat parts; its dust is strongly coloured and stains skin and clothing.

hazards.summary: A worker developed occupational asthma from padauk dust, confirmed by a specific inhalation challenge that also caused a marked rise in eosinophils (allergy-type white cells) in the airway.
A woodworker reacting to several exotic woods had a strong positive patch test to padauk sawdust, and an occupational allergic skin rash from Pterocarpus soyauxii has also been reported.
The UK HSE lists padauk as a reported cause of itching, eye irritation and swelling such as puffy eyelids, noting that effects depend on the species.
The UK HSE also lists vomiting among reported effects of padauk, again noting that it varies by species.
All wood dust is classified as carcinogenic to humans, mainly linked to cancers of the nose and sinuses after long-term exposure. This applies to this wood like any other.

exposure_limits.note: Applies to wood dust generally; this species has no separate ACGIH value.

related_species_note: Several Pterocarpus species are sold as padauk (e.g. Andaman padauk, P. dalbergioides, which has its own dermatitis report: Mehta 2007, PMID 17343633). Kejaat/muninga (Pterocarpus angolensis) has its own page.
image_prompt: Photorealistic studio photograph of a freshly planed African padauk (Pterocarpus soyauxii) board, shot at a low three-quarter angle so the face grain fills most of the frame. Freshly cut heartwood a vivid saturated orange-red to blood red with slightly darker reddish-brown streaks; no sapwood visible. Straight to slightly interlocked grain, medium to coarse texture with prominent open pores, a moderate natural luster. Soft diffused daylight from upper left, gentle falloff, neutral warm-grey seamless background, shallow depth of field with the near edge tack-sharp. No text, no logos, no hands, no tools, no finish or varnish, natural unfinished wood. Wide 1200x630 composition (1.91:1) with the board centered and margin on both sides for cropping.
image_alt: Planed board of African padauk with vivid orange-red heartwood and open pores.
notes_internal: Doyen-2023 full text not read; SIC confirmation from UCLouvain repository/search summaries, botanical name not confirmed in the paper. Rackett-1997 abstract names 'padauk' without species. KiecSwierczynska-2004 no abstract; title names P. soyauxii. HSE-WIS30 says 'species-dependant' and gives no botanical name. Li 2018 (PMID 29693067) reports carpenter's pigmentation from African padauk dust; not added. Common names barwood/camwood not verified against a Tier D source.
